event.title: Awareness Outbreak
event.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa, a politician from the ruling UDPS party in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was beaten on Sunday after advocating for Ebola awareness during a radio interview. The incident occurred in Butembo, a region experiencing an Ebola outbreak, as residents reacted violently to his message promoting disease prevention measures.

timeline.title: Mobile Labs Enhance Ebola Testing Efficiency in Eastern DR Congo
timeline.summary: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, has been operational for two weeks, significantly reducing the time required for Ebola test results. Previously, results took up to 72 hours, but the new facility can provide results within 24 hours, and in some cases, as quickly as six hours. This improvement is a relief for staff at the nearby Ebola treatment center.

timeline.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 4,000 deaths, according to health authorities. Efforts to control the epidemic are hampered by violence and public mistrust, exemplified by the recent burning of an Ebola-hit transit camp, which forced 19,000 people to flee.

timeline.summary: Kenya has confirmed its first-ever case of Ebola, resulting in the death of a man who had recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Health authorities have identified 28 contacts of the deceased as they monitor the situation closely. The outbreak in the DRC has been severe, with over 4,000 deaths reported this year.

timeline.title: Children Bear Heavy Toll in DRC's Severe Ebola Outbreak
timeline.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing its deadliest Ebola outbreak, with children particularly affected. Reports indicate that more than 1 in 4 of the deaths are among children, who face a staggering 60% fatality rate. This outbreak is caused by a rare strain of the virus for which there is currently no approved treatment.

timeline.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Surpasses 10,000 Cases Amid Growing Concerns
timeline.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has exceeded 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly 4,900 reported deaths. This outbreak, driven by the Bundibugyo virus, is noted as the fastest-growing in history, raising alarms about potential spread to other African nations. Currently, there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments available for this strain of the virus.

timeline.title: Last Ebola Patients Depart Treatment Center in DR Congo
timeline.summary: A treatment center in Ituri province, DR Congo, celebrated the discharge of its last confirmed Ebola patients, marking the first time since May that the facility has had no active cases. Medical staff and local residents participated in a joyful celebration as the clinic, run by Médecins Sans Frontières, reached this significant milestone.

event_overview.title: About Awareness Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Awareness Outbreak
event_overview.summary: Awareness Outbreak refers to the 2026 Ebola disease emergency caused by Bundibugyo virus, first declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in May 2026 and centered initially in Ituri Province. The response has combined outbreak control measures—such as surveillance, testing, contact tracing, clinical care and cross-border preparedness—with community engagement intended to counter misinformation and improve acceptance of public-health measures.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: The DRC declared the outbreak on 15 May 2026; it remained an active emergency as of 27 October 2026.

facts.label: Disease agent
facts.value: The outbreak is Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, a species for which WHO reported no licensed vaccine or approved specific therapeutic at the time of the response.

facts.label: Geographic setting
facts.value: The event began in north-eastern DRC, with Ituri Province as the initial epicentre, and later involved wider cross-border preparedness and response in the region.

facts.label: International governance
facts.value: WHO determined on 17 May 2026 that the epidemic in the DRC and Uganda constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern under the International Health Regulations (2005), while not meeting the separate definition of a pandemic emergency.

facts.label: Response priorities
facts.value: WHO and national authorities have emphasized rapid case detection, laboratory testing, contact tracing, treatment readiness, infection prevention, community engagement and cross-border coordination; WHO has advised against restrictions on travel or trade with affected countries based on the available information.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights particular late-September and October developments, including awareness, testing, deaths and reported regional spread; it does not provide a complete case history, all response operations, or a definitive epidemiological record of the outbreak.
